meta.spec_reference: ISO/IEC 11172-3:1993 (MPEG-1 Audio) and ISO/IEC 13818-3:1998 (MPEG-2 Audio, low sampling frequency extension) for the frame headers; "ID3 tag version 2.3.0" informal standard (3 February 1999) and "ID3 tag version 2.4.0 - Main Structure / Native Frames" (1 November 2000) for ID3v2; the "ID3 made easy" ID3v1 / ID3v1.1 informal standard for the appended tag; the Xing/LAME and Fraunhofer VBRI conventions for variable-bitrate headers.

schema_extensions.name: branch_variants
schema_extensions.why: The schema keys constraints as STRUCT.field, but this template declares the same field name two or three times in mutually exclusive branches of one struct, with different widths and different length expressions each time. A JSON object cannot hold duplicate keys, so a single entry carries an array of variants, each with its own verbatim declaration line, width or length expression, and the condition that selects it. Dropping the extra declarations would have lost the ID3v1.0/1.1 comment width difference and the size-versus-size-minus-one frame payload rule.

schema_extensions.name: unnamed_bitfields
schema_extensions.why: Four anonymous padding bitfields carry a real must-be-zero constraint but have no identifier in the .bt, so no STRUCT.field key can name them without inventing a field name, which the hard rules forbid. They are recorded as a separate array keyed by container struct, bit width and line, preserving the constraint without fabricating a name.

schema_extensions.name: lookahead_pools
schema_extensions.why: This template declares six FormatFuzzer value-pool locals (lines 112, 329, 330, 331, 486, 496). These are precisely the compile-time mined value sets the prompt calls the highest-value entries, but they are file-scope locals rather than fields, so the per-field lookahead key cannot express which pool feeds which call site. The section records each pool's declaration, its values, every consuming site and whether the pooled values are actually productive - two of the six pools are not.

schema_extensions.name: template_deviations
schema_extensions.why: Fifteen places where the template's field layout or arithmetic disagrees with the published specification, including two the template's own header comment documents as bugs. The rewrite step must follow the specification rather than the template for each of these, so they need to be machine-readable rather than buried in description prose.

schema_extensions.name: values_pool
schema_extensions.why: Records the <values=...> attribute attached to a field, the pool's declared contents and, where they disagree with the field's legal set, the specific problem. bitrate_index_values in particular pools two values the template itself rejects, which a generator must not inherit.

schema_extensions.name: valid_results and valid_results_names
schema_extensions.why: The field is simultaneously a length (so the schema requires calculated_value with algorithm, covers and includes_self) and a two-valued enumeration fixed by the specification. Rather than choosing one type and losing the other fact, the calculated_value entry carries the permitted results alongside.

schema_extensions.name: bitfield_layout
schema_extensions.where: every bitfield entry in FLAGS, FRAME_FLAGS, ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER and MPEG_HEADER
schema_extensions.why: BigEndian() is in effect from line 484 and the whole MPEG header is one uint32 of bitfields, so which physical bit a named flag occupies is decided by declaration order rather than by anything in the field name. A generator writing bytes rather than bitfields needs the mask.

schema_extensions.name: byte_layout, array_length_algorithm, array_length_range, known_values, evidence.line and evidence.snippet on spec-sourced entries
schema_extensions.where: synchsafe_integer.raw; ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_padding; the two frame id entries; spec-sourced entries and dependencies throughout
schema_extensions.why: byte_layout gives the seven-bit packing of a synchsafe integer; array_length_algorithm and array_length_range let an array carry both a content constraint (all zero) and a separate length rule; known_values lists real-world frame identifiers that constrain nothing formally but strongly affect whether a decoder does anything with the frame. Spec-sourced entries keep a line and snippet in addition to the required note wherever the template does declare the field, so every rule stays anchored to a real location in the file.

meta.structure_note: An MP3 file has no container, no length prefix at file level and no terminator: it is an optional ID3v2 tag at offset 0, then a bare stream of self-delimiting MPEG audio frames laid end to end, then an optional 128-byte ID3v1 tag anchored to the end of the file. Each frame's length is derived from its own four-byte header, so the only thing marking one frame's end is the next frame's eleven-bit sync pattern appearing exactly there - which makes frame-length arithmetic, not any single magic value, the format's real structural anchor.

synchsafe_integer.raw.description: The four bytes of an ID3v2 synchsafe integer; every byte must have its most significant bit clear, so each byte is 0-127 and the four together carry only 28 bits of magnitude.
synchsafe_integer.raw.byte_layout: raw[0] is the most significant group of 7 bits and raw[3] the least; value = ((((raw[0]<<7)|raw[1])<<7|raw[2])<<7)|raw[3], exactly as computed on lines 65-71.

generation_range.rationale: Per byte. A synchsafe byte of 0x80 or more is what the template's own warning on line 76 flags; setting the high bit also risks creating a false MPEG frame sync (0xFF followed by >=0xE0) inside the tag header, which is the exact failure unsynchronisation exists to prevent.

synchsafe_integer.raw.notes: Used for ID3v2_HEADER.size and for ID3v2_4_FRAME.size. ID3v2.3 frame sizes are NOT synchsafe (plain uint32) - see ID3v2_FRAME.size.

ID3v1_TAG.id.description: ID3v1 tag signature; the three ASCII bytes 'TAG' that open the final 128 bytes of the file.

lookahead.note: 0x5441 is 'TA' read big-endian; line 507 then confirms the third byte with ReadUByte(seek_pos+2) == 0x47 ('G').

ID3v1_TAG.id.notes: The main scan loop treats this signature as one of only two ways to leave the sync search (the other being a value >= 0xFFE0). Detected two bytes at a time on line 505 plus one byte on line 507.

ID3v1_TAG.title.pattern: ^[\x20-\xFF]{0,30}\x00*$ - up to 30 ISO-8859-1 characters, right-padded with 0x00 (0x20 is also seen in the wild); no length prefix and no terminator is required when all 30 bytes are used
ID3v1_TAG.title.description: Song title, a fixed 30-byte ISO-8859-1 field padded with zero bytes.
ID3v1_TAG.title.notes: ID3v1 has no encoding byte; the charset is fixed at ISO-8859-1 by the specification. Content is free text, but the padding convention and the absence of any escape mean an embedded 0xFF/0xE0 pair here cannot create a false frame sync only because this field sits after all MPEG data.

ID3v1_TAG.artist.pattern: ^[\x20-\xFF]{0,30}\x00*$ - up to 30 ISO-8859-1 characters, zero-padded to exactly 30 bytes
ID3v1_TAG.artist.description: Performing artist, a fixed 30-byte zero-padded ISO-8859-1 field.

ID3v1_TAG.album.pattern: ^[\x20-\xFF]{0,30}\x00*$ - up to 30 ISO-8859-1 characters, zero-padded to exactly 30 bytes
ID3v1_TAG.album.description: Album title, a fixed 30-byte zero-padded ISO-8859-1 field.

ID3v1_TAG.year.pattern: ^([0-9]{4}|\x00{4}|\x20{4})$ - four ASCII decimal digits, or four zero/space bytes when unknown
ID3v1_TAG.year.description: Four-character release year; the specification permits only ASCII digits, so a non-digit here is a spec violation the template never checks.
ID3v1_TAG.year.notes: No century marker and no room for one; this is a literal four-digit year, not an offset.

ID3v1_TAG.comment.pattern: ^[\x20-\xFF]*\x00*$ - ISO-8859-1 text zero-padded to the full field width, which is 30 bytes for ID3v1.0 and 28 bytes for ID3v1.1
ID3v1_TAG.comment.description: Free comment text whose width depends on the tag version: 28 bytes when an ID3v1.1 track number follows, 30 bytes otherwise.
ID3v1_TAG.comment.notes: Two separate declarations of the same field name in mutually exclusive branches of one struct, so a single key covers both; see branch_variants. Choosing the 28-byte form is what makes the track number reachable.

ID3v1_TAG.zero.description: The ID3v1.1 separator byte at offset 125 of the tag; it must be zero, and it is the sole marker distinguishing an ID3v1.1 tag from an ID3v1.0 tag whose comment happens to be 29 characters long.

lookahead.note: ReadByte(FTell()+28) == 0 is the test that selects this branch; the byte it inspects is this field.

ID3v1_TAG.zero.notes: A non-zero byte here silently reinterprets the last three bytes of the tag as comment text, losing the track number.

ID3v1_TAG.track.description: ID3v1.1 track number; must be non-zero, because a zero here is exactly the condition that makes the tag an ID3v1.0 tag instead.

generation_range.rationale: Real track numbers on an album; values above about 30 are legal but never occur, and 0 is forbidden by the branch condition on line 133.

lookahead.note: ReadByte(FTell()+29) != 0 inspects this field; the compared literal is 0 and the field must differ from it.

ID3v1_TAG.track.notes: This is the second half of the ID3v1.1 discriminator: zero byte at 125 AND non-zero byte at 126.

ID3v1_TAG.genre.description: Genre index into the ID3v1 genre table; the template's ID3_GENRES enum defines 0-147 and 255 means 'unset'.
ID3v1_TAG.genre.notes: Values 0-79 are the original Winamp list; 80-147 are the Winamp extensions the template also carries. 148-254 are undefined and 255 (0xFF) is the conventional 'no genre' marker, neither of which appears in the enum - see the dependency covering 255.

ID3v2_HEADER.head.description: ID3v2 tag signature; the three ASCII bytes 'ID3' that must sit at file offset 0 for a prepended tag to be recognised.

lookahead.note: ReadBytes(buf, 0, 3, buf_values) with buf_values declared on line 486 as { "ID3" }; the absolute offset 0 in the call is what pins the tag to the start of the file.

ID3v2_HEADER.head.notes: This is the single highest-value anchor in the format for FormatFuzzer: the value pool on line 486 is a compile-time mined set of exactly one string, and the comparison on line 490 is the only gate on the entire ID3v2 branch.

ID3v2_HEADER.ver_major.description: ID3v2 major version; the specification defines 2, 3 and 4, this template parses only 3 and 4 structurally, and the value 0xFF is explicitly forbidden.

evidence.snippet: ubyte ver_major; // this byte will never be $FF

ID3v2_HEADER.ver_major.notes: Line 289 rejects 0xFF outright and line 295 diverts anything other than 3 or 4 into an opaque id3v2_data blob, so generating 2 produces a file the template will not walk into. Version 3 is the most widely supported by real decoders and keeps frame sizes as plain integers.

ID3v2_HEADER.ver_revision.description: ID3v2 minor revision; every published ID3v2 revision is 0, and the template pins the field to 0 with an initial-value list.

evidence.snippet: ubyte ver_revision = { 0 }; // this byte will never be $FF

ID3v2_HEADER.ver_revision.notes: The '= { 0 }' suffix is a value list, so a generator should emit 0. The specification's only hard rule is that this byte is never 0xFF (line 289 enforces exactly that); values 1-254 are structurally parseable but no such revision exists.

FLAGS.UNSYNCHRONISATION_USED.description: Bit 7 of the ID3v2 header flags; when set, every 0xFF byte in the tag body has been followed by an inserted 0x00 so that no false MPEG frame sync can occur inside the tag.
FLAGS.UNSYNCHRONISATION_USED.bitfield_layout: Declared first in struct FLAGS, so under BigEndian() it occupies the most significant bit (0x80) of the flags byte.
FLAGS.UNSYNCHRONISATION_USED.notes: Setting this bit without actually performing the unsynchronisation scheme makes every declared frame size wrong, because the sizes describe the unsynchronised (encoded) bytes. Line 295 makes the template abandon structural parsing when this bit is set, so 0 is the only productive value.

FLAGS.EXTENDED_HEADER_PRESENT.description: Bit 6 of the ID3v2 header flags; when set, an ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER must immediately follow the ten-byte header.
FLAGS.EXTENDED_HEADER_PRESENT.bitfield_layout: Second bit declared, so mask 0x40 of the flags byte.
FLAGS.EXTENDED_HEADER_PRESENT.notes: This is a presence flag, not a hint: setting it with no extended header present shifts every subsequent frame by at least ten bytes.

FLAGS.EXPERIMENTAL_TAG.description: Bit 5 of the ID3v2 header flags, marking the tag as an experimental stage tag.
FLAGS.EXPERIMENTAL_TAG.bitfield_layout: Third bit declared, so mask 0x20 of the flags byte.
FLAGS.EXPERIMENTAL_TAG.notes: Purely advisory in the specification, but line 295 treats it exactly like unsynchronisation and refuses to parse frames, so 0 is required to reach any frame structure.

ID3v2_HEADER.size.covers: every byte of the tag after the ten-byte header, that is the extended header if present plus all frames plus all padding, and excluding the header itself and excluding any ID3v2.4 footer
ID3v2_HEADER.size.description: Total size of the ID3v2 tag body; equals total tag size minus 10, stored as a synchsafe integer so no byte reaches 0x80.

evidence.snippet: synchsafe_integer size; // Is the size of the complete tag after unsynchronisation,

generation_range.rationale: The synchsafe encoding permits up to 2^28-1 (256 MB) of tag body. A tag larger than a few kilobytes is pure padding or embedded artwork and only slows generation; the true maximum stays in the algorithm, this is the practical cap. The minimum of 11 reflects the specification's rule that a tag contains at least one frame and a frame is at least one byte beyond its ten-byte header.

ID3v2_HEADER.size.notes: Line 282 copies this into the local tag_sz and lines 321 and 324 both use 'tag_sz + sizeof(hdr)', where sizeof(hdr) is 10, to locate the end of the tag. Getting this wrong does not corrupt the tag alone: it relocates where the MPEG frame scan begins.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.size.algorithm: byte count, plain big-endian uint32 (NOT synchsafe in ID3v2.3)
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.size.covers: the extended header bytes that follow this field: the two-byte extended flags, the four-byte padding_sz, and the four-byte crc when present; it excludes this size field itself
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.size.description: Length of the remainder of the ID3v2.3 extended header; the specification permits exactly two values, 6 without a CRC and 10 with one.

evidence.snippet: uint32 size; // extended header size, excluding this 'size' field

generation_range.rationale: The only two legal values; any other makes the tag body length disagree with the frames that follow.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.size.notes: This is both a length and a two-valued enumeration, which is why valid_results is carried alongside the calculated_value keys. Note that the template reads it as a plain uint32, which is correct for ID3v2.3 but wrong for ID3v2.4, where the extended header size is synchsafe and includes itself.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.FLAG_CRC_PRESENT.description: Bit 15 of the extended header flags word; when set, a four-byte CRC follows padding_sz and the extended header size must be 10.
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.FLAG_CRC_PRESENT.bitfield_layout: Declared first in a uint16 under BigEndian(), so it is the most significant bit of the two-byte flags word, mask 0x8000.
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.FLAG_CRC_PRESENT.notes: Controls both a field's presence (line 199) and the legal value of ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.size; the two must agree or the frame stream starts four bytes off.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.padding_sz.algorithm: byte count of the zero padding that trails the frames inside the tag
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.padding_sz.covers: the run of 0x00 bytes between the last frame and the end of the tag body, which the template reads as ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_padding
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.padding_sz.description: Declared number of padding bytes inside the tag; it must equal the actual trailing zero run, and it is counted inside ID3v2_HEADER.size.

generation_range.rationale: A uint32 nominally reaches 4294967295 and the specification's only bound is that padding fits inside the tag. Real files use a kilobyte or so to allow in-place tag editing; anything larger is dead bytes that inflate every generated file.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.padding_sz.notes: The specification requires padding to be entirely zero bytes and forbids it after an ID3v2.4 footer. Because the template computes the actual padding length on line 324 from tag_sz rather than from this field, a mismatch here is invisible to the template but breaks conforming readers.

ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.crc.algorithm: CRC-32/ISO-HDLC (the ISO 3309 / ITU-T V.42 polynomial 0x04C11DB7, as used by ZIP and PNG)
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.crc.covers: all frames and all padding inside the tag, that is everything between the end of the extended header and the end of the tag body; it excludes the ten-byte header and the whole extended header
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.crc.description: Optional CRC-32 over the tag's frame data and padding, present only when FLAG_CRC_PRESENT is set.
ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER.crc.notes: No reader is obliged to verify this, which is why the risk is medium rather than high; but a conforming reader that does verify will discard the entire tag on a mismatch. Generating a wrong CRC is a genuinely interesting fuzz input, hence evil_bit_safe true.

FRAME_FLAGS.TAG_ALTER_PRESERV.description: Tag alter preservation flag; when set, a reader that alters the tag must discard this frame.
FRAME_FLAGS.TAG_ALTER_PRESERV.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x8000 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag a.

FRAME_FLAGS.FILE_ALTER_PRESERV.description: File alter preservation flag; when set, a reader that alters the audio data must discard this frame.
FRAME_FLAGS.FILE_ALTER_PRESERV.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x4000 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag b.

FRAME_FLAGS.READ_ONLY_FRAME.description: Read-only flag; the frame contents are not intended to be changed.
FRAME_FLAGS.READ_ONLY_FRAME.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x2000 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag c.

FRAME_FLAGS.COMPRESSED_FRAME.description: Compression flag; when set, the frame data is zlib-compressed and is preceded by a four-byte big-endian decompressed size, which the template does not read.
FRAME_FLAGS.COMPRESSED_FRAME.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x0080 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag i.
FRAME_FLAGS.COMPRESSED_FRAME.notes: Setting this bit changes the frame's internal layout: the specification prepends a four-byte 'decompressed size' before the compressed bytes, so the template's frame_data array silently swallows it. Generating 1 here without that prefix produces a frame no conforming decoder can read.

FRAME_FLAGS.ENCRYPTED_FRAME.description: Encryption flag; when set, the frame data is preceded by a one-byte encryption method identifier which the template does not read.
FRAME_FLAGS.ENCRYPTED_FRAME.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x0040 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag j.
FRAME_FLAGS.ENCRYPTED_FRAME.notes: Like compression, this bit adds a prefix byte the template does not account for. It also requires a matching ENCR frame elsewhere in the tag to define the method.

FRAME_FLAGS.GROUP_MEMBER_FRAME.description: Grouping flag; when set, the frame data is preceded by a one-byte group identifier which the template does not read.
FRAME_FLAGS.GROUP_MEMBER_FRAME.bitfield_layout: Bit 0x0020 of the two-byte ID3v2.3 frame flags word under BigEndian(); the word is %abc00000 %ijk00000 and this is flag k.
FRAME_FLAGS.GROUP_MEMBER_FRAME.notes: Requires a matching GRID frame in the same tag to define the group symbol.

ID3v2_FRAME.id.pattern: ^[A-Z0-9]{4}$ - exactly four characters drawn from the capital letters A-Z and the digits 0-9; identifiers beginning with 'X', 'Y' or 'Z' are reserved for experimental use
ID3v2_FRAME.id.description: Four-character ID3v2.3 frame identifier; the template's comment calls them 'four alpha chars' and the specification restricts them to upper-case letters and digits.
ID3v2_FRAME.id.notes: The template branches on id[0] == 'T' (line 229) alone, so any identifier starting with 'T' is treated as a text frame and given a leading encoding byte. A frame identifier of four zero bytes is how readers detect the start of padding, so all-zero is not a legal identifier but is the conventional end-of-frames signal - see the loop condition on line 321.

ID3v2_FRAME.size.algorithm: byte count, plain big-endian uint32 (ID3v2.3 frame sizes are NOT synchsafe)
ID3v2_FRAME.size.covers: the frame's data bytes only: everything after the ten-byte frame header, excluding the four-byte identifier, this size field and the two flag bytes; when the compression, encryption or grouping flags are set it also covers the extra prefix bytes those flags introduce
ID3v2_FRAME.size.description: Size of this frame's data excluding its ten-byte header; the specification requires it to be at least 1.

evidence.snippet: uint32 size; // frame size without frame header

generation_range.rationale: The field is a full uint32, so the spec bound is 4294967295 - a single frame could claim four gigabytes. The template allocates frame_data of exactly this length on lines 235, 238 and 243, so an uncapped value produces an enormous array and dominates runtime. Real text frames are tens of bytes; 256 covers everything but embedded artwork. The minimum of 1 is the specification's own rule (see the comment on lines 308-309).

ID3v2_FRAME.size.notes: A crucial difference from ID3v2_4_FRAME.size, which is synchsafe. Emitting a v2.3 frame size as synchsafe, or a v2.4 size as plain, shifts every following frame.

ID3v2_FRAME.id_asciiz_str.description: The text-encoding byte at the head of a text frame; the template only takes this branch when the byte is already zero, which is ISO-8859-1.

lookahead.note: ReadByte(FTell()) == 0 && size > 1 is the guard on line 232; the byte it reads is this field.

ID3v2_FRAME.id_asciiz_str.notes: Really the ID3v2.3 text encoding byte, whose legal values are 0 (ISO-8859-1) and 1 (UTF-16 with BOM). The template's branch structure means a value of 1 is parsed as the first character of frame_data instead, so only 0 keeps the template's field layout and the specification's layout in agreement.

ID3v2_FRAME.frame_data.algorithm: array length derived from the frame header: size for a non-text frame or a text frame whose first byte is non-zero, and size - 1 for a text frame whose encoding byte was consumed separately
ID3v2_FRAME.frame_data.covers: the frame payload bytes that follow the ten-byte frame header and, in the text-frame case, the one encoding byte
ID3v2_FRAME.frame_data.description: The frame payload; its content is free but its length is fully determined by size and by whether the encoding byte was split off.

branch_variants.condition: id[0] == 'T' and the next byte is 0 and size > 1
id[0] == 'T' but the next byte is not 0, or size <= 1

ID3v2_FRAME.frame_data.notes: Three declarations of one field name across mutually exclusive branches of a single struct, so one key covers all three; see branch_variants. Payload content is free-form, but the length identity is not, and it is the identity that keeps the frame stream aligned.

ID3v2_4_FRAME.id.pattern: ^[A-Z0-9]{4}$ - exactly four characters drawn from A-Z and 0-9
ID3v2_4_FRAME.id.description: Four-character ID3v2.4 frame identifier, same character set as ID3v2.3 but with a partly different set of defined identifiers.
ID3v2_4_FRAME.id.notes: ID3v2.4 replaced TYER/TDAT/TIME with the single TDRC and dropped several v2.3 identifiers; a v2.3-only identifier inside a v2.4 tag is structurally parseable but semantically invalid.

ID3v2_4_FRAME.size.covers: the frame's data bytes only, excluding the ten-byte frame header; for a text frame this includes the one-byte encoding field, which is why the template reads size.computed - 1 payload bytes after it
ID3v2_4_FRAME.size.description: Size of this ID3v2.4 frame's data excluding its header, stored as a synchsafe integer so that no byte reaches 0x80.

evidence.snippet: synchsafe_integer size; // frame size without frame header

generation_range.rationale: The synchsafe encoding tops out at 2^28-1, so a single frame could claim 256 MB and the template would allocate exactly that on line 268 or 273. Real frames are tens of bytes. The floor of 1 is the specification's minimum frame data size, and for a text frame the encoding byte alone already requires size >= 1.

ID3v2_4_FRAME.size.notes: The change from v2.3's plain uint32 to a synchsafe integer is the single most consequential difference between the two frame layouts, and it is why the template needs two separate frame structs at all.

ID3v2_4_FRAME.encoding.description: Text encoding byte that opens every ID3v2.4 text frame; the four values are exactly the encodings ID3v2.4 defines.
ID3v2_4_FRAME.encoding.notes: Values 4-255 are undefined and cause conforming readers to reject the frame. ISO-8859-1 is preferred because it needs no BOM and one byte per character, so the frame data has no further internal structure to satisfy. Note ID3v2.3 defines only values 0 and 1; encodings 2 and 3 are new in v2.4.

ID3v2_4_FRAME.frame_data.algorithm: array length derived from the synchsafe frame size: size.computed - 1 for a text frame, whose one encoding byte has already been consumed, and size.computed for a binary frame
ID3v2_4_FRAME.frame_data.covers: the frame payload bytes that follow the ten-byte frame header and, for a text frame, the encoding byte
ID3v2_4_FRAME.frame_data.description: The ID3v2.4 frame payload; free content, but a length wholly determined by the synchsafe size field and the frame's text/binary branch.

branch_variants.condition: id[0] == 'T' - a text frame, after the encoding byte

ID3v2_4_FRAME.frame_data.notes: Unlike the ID3v2.3 branch, this one has no 'size > 1' guard, so a text frame declaring size 0 makes the template request an array of length -1.

ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_data.algorithm: array length equal to the tag body size taken verbatim from the header's synchsafe size field
ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_data.covers: the entire tag body of an ID3v2 version the template will not walk into: everything after the ten-byte header, read as opaque bytes
ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_data.description: Opaque fallback array covering a whole tag body whenever the version is not 3 or 4, or unsynchronisation or the experimental flag is set.

generation_range.rationale: Inherits the practical cap on ID3v2_HEADER.size; the array is allocated at exactly that length.

ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_data.notes: Reaching this branch means no frame structure is generated at all, which is why ver_major 3 or 4 with clear unsynchronisation and experimental flags is strongly preferred.

ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_padding.description: Zero padding filling the gap between the last frame and the end of the tag body; the specification requires every padding byte to be 0x00.
ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_padding.array_length_algorithm: tag_sz + sizeof(hdr) - FTell(), where tag_sz is ID3v2_HEADER.size.computed and sizeof(hdr) is 10; that is, whatever is left of the declared tag body after the frames have been read

generation_range.rationale: The declared tag size can leave an arbitrarily large padding run. A kilobyte matches real files that reserve room for later tag edits; larger runs are dead weight in every generated file. Note the expression is unsigned, so if the frames overshoot the declared tag size this length underflows to a near-4GB array.

ID3v2_TAG.id3v2_padding.notes: A non-zero byte here is what stops a conforming reader early: padding is defined as a run of zeroes, and the first non-zero byte is taken as the start of a frame identifier. This is the same rule the template's own loop exit on line 321 relies on.

MPEG_HEADER.frame_sync.description: The template's twelve-bit sync field: the eleven mandatory frame-sync bits, which must all be 1, plus the high bit of the two-bit MPEG version field that follows them.
MPEG_HEADER.frame_sync.bitfield_layout: Declared first in a uint32 under BigEndian(), so it occupies the top twelve bits of the four header bytes: all eight bits of byte 0 and the top four bits of byte 1. The header as a whole is AAAAAAAA AAABBCCD EEEEFFGH IIJJKLMM (comment on line 334), where A is the eleven-bit sync and BB the version; this field is AAAAAAAAAAA plus the first B.

lookahead.note: The scan loop reads a big-endian ushort and accepts the frame when data >= 0xFFE0 (lines 510, 518, 520). The declared value pool on line 496 contains only 0x5441, the ID3v1 'TA' signature, so FormatFuzzer mines no sync value from this call site at all - the >= 0xFFE0 threshold is a range test, not an equality, and never contributes a literal.

generation_range.rationale: 0xFFE means the two-bit version is 00 or 01, that is MPEG 2.5 or the reserved version. The template does not support MPEG 2.5 at all (TODO on line 29) and the reserved version is invalid outright, so only 0xFFF yields a frame both the template and a real decoder will accept.

MPEG_HEADER.frame_sync.notes: This is the anchor that makes a file an MP3 at all, and the one bit pattern a generator must never perturb. A 'sync' of 0xFFE0 or greater is all this parser demands, but the specification requires eleven set bits followed by a version that is not 01.

MPEG_HEADER.mpeg_id.description: The low bit of the two-bit MPEG version field; combined with the low bit of frame_sync it gives version 00 = MPEG 2.5, 01 = reserved, 10 = MPEG-2, 11 = MPEG-1.
MPEG_HEADER.mpeg_id.bitfield_layout: Bit B (the second of the two version bits) at mask 0x00080000 of the big-endian header word.

values_pool.problem: The pool declares 2, which a one-bit field cannot hold; only the value 1 in that pool is reachable.

MPEG_HEADER.mpeg_id.notes: Selects the sampling-frequency table (line 442 doubles the frequency for MPEG-1) and, for Layer III, the whole bitrate table (lines 402 and 408). MPEG-1 is preferred because it is what every decoder supports and what the template's frame-size arithmetic is tuned for.

MPEG_HEADER.layer_id.description: Two-bit layer selector; 0 is reserved and rejected by the template's own sanity check, 1 is Layer III, 2 is Layer II and 3 is Layer I.
MPEG_HEADER.layer_id.bitfield_layout: Bits CC at mask 0x00060000 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.layer_id.notes: Line 375 rejects layer_id == 0 explicitly. Layer III is preferred: it is what the .mp3 extension means, and it is the branch the template's most-developed bitrate arithmetic covers (lines 402-428). Note the encoding is inverted relative to the layer number - layer 3 in the field means Layer I.

value_names: CRC protected - a 16-bit checksum follows the header
MPEG_HEADER.protection_bit.description: Protection bit; the sense is inverted, so 0 means a CRC-16 checksum follows the four header bytes and 1 means no checksum.
MPEG_HEADER.protection_bit.bitfield_layout: Bit D at mask 0x00010000 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.protection_bit.notes: A presence flag, not a hint: it decides whether MPEG_HEADER.checksum exists (line 359) and it shifts every frame-size computation by two bytes (lines 380, 450, 452). Value 1 is preferred because it removes the need to compute a correct CRC-16 over the header and side information.

MPEG_HEADER.bitrate_index.description: Four-bit index into the bitrate table selected by version and layer; 0 means 'free format' and 15 is defined as invalid, and the template rejects both.
MPEG_HEADER.bitrate_index.bitfield_layout: Bits EEEE at mask 0x0000F000 of the big-endian header word.

values_pool.problem: Two of the three pooled values, 0 and 15, are exactly the two the sanity check on line 376 rejects; a generator seeded from this pool produces an invalid header two times in three.

generation_range.rationale: Not a size cap but a validity cap: index 0 selects free-format, where the bitrate is not in the header at all and the frame length must be inferred from the next sync, which the template cannot do (it computes bitrate = 0 and then skips the frame body entirely). Index 15 is the reserved 'bad' value.

MPEG_HEADER.bitrate_index.notes: Index 9 is 128 kbit/s for MPEG-1 Layer III, the most common real-world value; it gives an integral frame size of 417 or 418 bytes at 44.1 kHz. The whole of lines 387-431 is the version-and-layer-dependent decode of this index.

value_names: 44100 Hz for MPEG-1, 22050 Hz for MPEG-2
48000 Hz for MPEG-1, 24000 Hz for MPEG-2
32000 Hz for MPEG-1, 16000 Hz for MPEG-2
MPEG_HEADER.frequency_index.description: Two-bit sampling-frequency index; value 3 is reserved and is rejected by the template's sanity check.
MPEG_HEADER.frequency_index.bitfield_layout: Bits FF at mask 0x00000C00 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.frequency_index.notes: Line 377 rejects value 3, and line 440 would index one past the end of the three-element freq[] table if it did not. The stored table on lines 436-438 holds the frequencies divided by ten; line 443 doubles them for MPEG-1.

MPEG_HEADER.padding_bit.description: Padding bit; when set the frame carries one extra slot so that the average bitrate is met exactly - one byte for Layers II and III, four bytes for Layer I.
MPEG_HEADER.padding_bit.bitfield_layout: Bit G at mask 0x00000200 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.padding_bit.notes: Directly changes the frame length (line 450 subtracts it), so it is a length input, not a flag a decoder may ignore. Note the template adds exactly one byte for a set padding bit regardless of layer, which is wrong for Layer I.

MPEG_HEADER.channel_mode.description: Two-bit channel mode; all four values are legal, but mono halves the frame size and constrains which bitrates Layer II may use.
MPEG_HEADER.channel_mode.bitfield_layout: Bits II at mask 0x000000C0 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.channel_mode.notes: Line 447 halves frame_size when this is 3 (mono), which is the source of the template's own documented bug for MPEG-1 Layer III mono at low bitrates (lines 33-35). The name mapping is confirmed by the Printf on lines 545-547.

value_names: Layers I/II: subbands 4-31; Layer III: intensity off, MS off
Layers I/II: subbands 8-31; Layer III: intensity on, MS off
Layers I/II: subbands 12-31; Layer III: intensity off, MS on
Layers I/II: subbands 16-31; Layer III: intensity on, MS on
MPEG_HEADER.mode_extension.description: Two-bit joint-stereo mode extension; meaningful only when channel_mode is 1 (joint stereo), and its meaning differs between Layer III and Layers I/II.
MPEG_HEADER.mode_extension.bitfield_layout: Bits JJ at mask 0x00000030 of the big-endian header word.
MPEG_HEADER.mode_extension.notes: The specification requires this field to be 0 when channel_mode is not joint stereo. The template never reads it, so a non-zero value in a stereo or mono frame is invisible here but is a conformance error a real decoder may act on.

MPEG_HEADER.emphasis.description: Two-bit de-emphasis selector; value 2 is reserved and must not appear.
MPEG_HEADER.emphasis.bitfield_layout: Bits MM at mask 0x00000003 of the big-endian header word, the last two bits of the fourth header byte.
MPEG_HEADER.emphasis.notes: The template's sanity check on lines 375-377 does not test emphasis, so the reserved value 2 passes unchallenged here while conforming decoders reject it. This is a pure spec-over-parser constraint.

MPEG_HEADER.checksum.algorithm: CRC-16 with polynomial x^16 + x^15 + x^2 + 1 (0x8005), initial value 0xFFFF, no final XOR
MPEG_HEADER.checksum.covers: the last two bytes of the four-byte frame header, that is bytes 2 and 3 holding bitrate_index through emphasis, followed by the side-information bytes at the start of the frame data; it excludes the first two header bytes carrying the sync, version, layer and protection bit, and excludes the checksum itself
MPEG_HEADER.checksum.description: Optional CRC-16 over the header tail and side information, present only when protection_bit is 0.
MPEG_HEADER.checksum.notes: The number of side-information bytes covered depends on version and channel mode: for Layer III it is 17 bytes for MPEG-1 mono, 32 for MPEG-1 non-mono, 9 for MPEG-2 mono and 17 for MPEG-2 non-mono. Most decoders skip verification and play the frame regardless, which is why the risk is medium; setting protection_bit to 1 removes the field and the obligation entirely.

MPEG_FRAME.mpeg_frame_data.algorithm: frame_size = (bitrate * 14400) / sampling_freq, halved when channel_mode is 3, then reduced by 4 header bytes plus 2 more when a checksum is present, then increased by the padding bit; sampling_freq is the tenth-of-a-hertz table value from lines 436-438, doubled for MPEG-1
MPEG_FRAME.mpeg_frame_data.covers: the audio payload of one MPEG frame: everything after the four header bytes and the optional two checksum bytes, up to the start of the next frame's sync word
MPEG_FRAME.mpeg_frame_data.description: One frame's audio data; its content is free, but its length is fully determined by the header fields and must place the next frame's sync word exactly at its end.

generation_range.rationale: Not a free choice - the length is derived - but the derived value must stay bounded, and it is bounded by the bitrate and frequency chosen. The extremes of the legal table are roughly 24 bytes (8 kbit/s MPEG-2 at 24 kHz) and 1440 bytes (320 kbit/s MPEG-1 Layer III at 32 kHz); a generator should keep the bitrate and frequency indices in ranges that land inside this window rather than emitting an arbitrary array length.

MPEG_FRAME.mpeg_frame_data.notes: The canonical formula for MPEG-1 Layer III is 144 * bitrate / samplerate + padding; the template's (bitrate * 14400) / sampling_freq is the same identity with the frequency held in tenths of a hertz. The mono halving on line 448 is the documented bug from lines 33-35 - it is not part of the specification and makes the template's own idea of the frame length wrong for MPEG-1 Layer III mono. Line 455 aborts parsing when the computed length would run past end of file, so the final frame must fit entirely inside the file.

structure.subject: Xing, Info or VBRI header inside the first MPEG_FRAME.mpeg_frame_data
structure.detail: for a variable-bitrate file the first frame's payload carries a Xing/Info header at a version-and-channel-dependent offset (17, 21 or 32 bytes past the header), or a VBRI header 32 bytes past it
structure.description: A convention rather than part of ISO/IEC 11172-3, but it is what makes VBR files seekable, and the template has no field for it - the bytes fall inside mpeg_frame_data.

evidence.note: Xing/LAME convention: the first frame of a VBR stream is a silent frame whose side-information area is followed by the ASCII tag 'Xing' or 'Info'; VBRI places 'VBRI' at a fixed offset of 32 bytes.

structure.generation_bound: at most one, in the first frame only
structure.generation_note: only relevant if generating VBR; for constant-bitrate output omit it entirely and keep every frame's bitrate_index identical

unnamed_bitfields.mask: 0x1F of the ID3v2 header flags byte
unnamed_bitfields.description: The low five bits of the ID3v2.3 header flags byte are reserved and must be cleared; the specification says a tag with any of them set should be discarded.

unnamed_bitfields.mask: 0x7FFF of the two-byte extended header flags word
unnamed_bitfields.description: All extended-header flag bits other than the CRC bit are reserved and must be zero.

unnamed_bitfields.mask: 0x1F00 of the frame flags word - the low five bits of the first flags byte
unnamed_bitfields.description: Reserved bits of the ID3v2.3 frame status flags byte; the specification requires them cleared.

unnamed_bitfields.mask: 0x001F of the frame flags word - the low five bits of the second flags byte
unnamed_bitfields.description: Reserved bits of the ID3v2.3 frame format flags byte; the specification requires them cleared.

consumed_by.decides: whether another ID3v2 frame follows or padding begins

lookahead_pools.note: A const global pool naming the two values every ReadByte site in this template compares against. Both are productive: 0 drives the ID3v1.1 and padding branches, 1 the alternatives.

consumed_by.decides: ID3v2_HEADER.head - whether an ID3v2 tag is parsed at all

lookahead_pools.note: The single highest-value mined literal in the file: the whole ID3v2 branch hangs on this three-byte comparison at absolute offset 0.

consumed_by.decides: ID3v1_TAG.id - 0x5441 is 'TA', confirmed as 'TAG' by the ReadUByte on line 507

lookahead_pools.note: This pool contains only the ID3v1 signature. Crucially it does NOT contain any MPEG sync value, because the sync test on lines 510/518/520 is a >= 0xFFE0 threshold rather than an equality - so no sync literal is mined here, and a generator seeded only from this pool will never produce a frame sync. This is the most consequential gap in the template's mineable value sets.
Attached to a one-bit field, so the value 2 is unrepresentable; only 1 is usable and 0 (MPEG-2) is absent from the pool.
Correct and complete for a one-bit field.

Actively harmful as a generation pool: 0 is free format and 15 is the reserved bad value, both rejected by the template's own check on line 376, so two of three pooled values guarantee an invalid frame.

template_deviations.deviation: frame_sync is declared as twelve bits, not eleven
template_deviations.detail: The MPEG frame sync is eleven bits. The template's twelve-bit field absorbs the high bit of the two-bit version field, which is why the sanity check compares against 0xFFE rather than 0x7FF and why mpeg_id is only one bit wide.
template_deviations.consequence: A generator that treats frame_sync as an opaque twelve-bit value and mpeg_id as a full version selector will produce version 01, the reserved encoding, whenever frame_sync is 0xFFE and mpeg_id is 1.

template_deviations.deviation: mpeg_id_values contains a value the field cannot hold
template_deviations.detail: The pool is { 1, 2 } but the field is one bit wide.
template_deviations.consequence: Value 2 is unreachable and value 0, meaning MPEG-2, is never suggested; the pool contributes exactly one usable literal.

template_deviations.detail: The pool is { 0, 1, 15 }; the template's own sanity check on line 376 rejects 0 and 15.
template_deviations.consequence: Seeding generation from this pool yields an invalid MPEG header two times in three; the correct generative set is 1 through 14.

template_deviations.deviation: no MPEG sync value is ever compared against a literal
template_deviations.detail: The sync test is the threshold data < 0xFFE0 rather than an equality, so no sync constant appears in any value pool.
template_deviations.consequence: FormatFuzzer mines no frame-sync literal from this template at all; the sync must come from the specification, which is why MPEG_HEADER.frame_sync carries an explicit generation_range pinned to 0xFFF.

template_deviations.deviation: frame size is halved for mono
template_deviations.detail: Line 447 halves frame_size when channel_mode is 3. No such rule exists in ISO/IEC 11172-3: the frame length depends on bitrate and sampling frequency only, not on channel count.
template_deviations.consequence: The template's own header comment on lines 33-35 documents this as a known bug for MPEG-1 Layer III mono. A generator that copies the template's arithmetic will place the next sync word at half the correct distance.

template_deviations.deviation: the padding slot is always one byte
template_deviations.detail: Line 450 adds mpeg_hdr.padding_bit to the length regardless of layer; a Layer I padding slot is four bytes.
template_deviations.consequence: Layer I frames with the padding bit set are three bytes short.

template_deviations.deviation: the ID3v2.4 frame flag layout is not implemented
template_deviations.detail: ID3v2_4_FRAME reuses FRAME_FLAGS, which encodes the ID3v2.3 layout %abc00000 %ijk00000. ID3v2.4 uses %0abc0000 %0h00kmnp, with every flag shifted one bit and new unsynchronisation and data-length-indicator flags added.
template_deviations.consequence: Every ID3v2.4 frame flag this template reports is one bit out of position, and the v2.4 data-length-indicator flag - which adds four bytes before the payload - is invisible.

template_deviations.deviation: the ID3v2.4 extended header layout is not implemented

evidence.snippet: uint32 size; // extended header size, excluding this 'size' field

template_deviations.detail: ID3v2_EXTENDED_HEADER reads a plain uint32 size, two flag bytes and a four-byte padding size. In ID3v2.4 the extended header size is synchsafe and includes itself, there is a flag-byte count, and padding_sz does not exist.
template_deviations.consequence: A version 4 tag with an extended header is parsed with version 3 field widths and every frame after it is misaligned.

template_deviations.deviation: the ID3v2.4 footer is not supported
template_deviations.detail: ID3v2.4 defines an optional ten-byte footer with the signature '3DI', flagged by bit 4 of the header flags byte - a bit the FLAGS struct folds into its anonymous five-bit remainder.
template_deviations.consequence: A footer is neither generated nor accounted for in the tag size, and its bytes would be scanned as audio.

template_deviations.detail: Rather than undoing the $FF $00 insertions, the template abandons frame parsing whenever the flag is set.
template_deviations.consequence: No unsynchronised tag ever exercises the frame structs, so setting that flag costs all frame coverage.

template_deviations.deviation: the ID3v1.1 discriminator is read from inside the comment field
template_deviations.detail: The lookahead at line 133 reads FTell()+28 and FTell()+29 while positioned at the start of the comment, so it inspects bytes that the ID3v1.0 branch would treat as comment text.
template_deviations.consequence: An ID3v1.0 comment whose 29th byte is zero and 30th is non-zero is misparsed as ID3v1.1; this is inherent to the format, not a template error, but a generator must choose the layout deliberately rather than letting comment bytes decide it.

template_deviations.deviation: the ID3v2 frame loop is a do-while
template_deviations.detail: The exit test on line 321 runs only after a frame has been read, so at least one frame is always parsed even when tag_sz is 0.
template_deviations.consequence: A tag declaring size 0 still consumes at least ten bytes of what should be audio, and line 324 then computes a padding length of 0 minus that, which underflows an unsigned expression.

template_deviations.deviation: no bounds check on ID3v2_4_FRAME text frames
template_deviations.detail: The v2.3 branch guards its size - 1 subtraction with 'size > 1' on line 232; the v2.4 branch has no equivalent guard.
template_deviations.consequence: A v2.4 text frame declaring size 0 requests an array of length -1.

template_deviations.detail: Listed as TODO item 1 in the template header. MPEG 2.5 uses version bits 00 and sampling frequencies of 11025, 12000 and 8000 Hz.
template_deviations.consequence: A frame_sync of 0xFFE with mpeg_id 0 is accepted by the sanity check but decoded with the wrong frequency table and the wrong frame-length divisor.

template_deviations.deviation: the sync search resynchronises by only two bytes
template_deviations.detail: On a failed sanity check the template seeks back to FTell() - 2 rather than to the byte after the false sync.
template_deviations.consequence: Recovery behaviour differs from a real decoder's byte-by-byte resync; a generated file with a near-miss sync will be walked differently by the template than by a player.
